newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firms ahead of T-bill, OFZ bond sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firms ahead of T-bill, OFZ bond sales.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Tuesday on shortages after the central bank's recent dollar interventions, and dealers said banks actively sought roubles to participate in Wednesday's government securities auctions.
Jan 21 midday Jan 21 early Jan 20 close
"Roubles have been getting expensive since Thursday as banks were buying dollars from the central bank agressively. Banks are attracted by tomorrow's auctions as well," one dealer said.
On Wednesday the central bank will auction 7.5 trillion roubles of nine-month Treasury bills and three trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ bonds.
Dealers said new taxation rules on T-bill operation profits led them to seek more roubles on the eve of Wednesday's sales.
Russia formally extended a profits tax to Treasury bill earnings on Tuesday with the official publication of an amendment to the profits tax law.
"Banks seem interested in the auctions and are counting on higher yields -- roubles are scarce because of that," ABN-Amro Bank chief dealer Dmitry Piskulov said.
